conventions.convention: Worldlines have interval domains with nonempty interior. Included endpoints use one-sided derivatives; piecewise C1 curves have finitely many pieces on each compact interval, with continuous derivative extensions on each closed piece and separate corner tangents.

For future timelike curves and c>0, proper-time density is sqrt(-g(γ′,γ′))/c, Lorentzian length is c times the proper-time increment, and U=cγ′/sqrt(-g(γ′,γ′)), so g(U,U)=-c². These mathematical definitions assign neither proper time nor four-velocity to null or spacelike curves.

Reparametrization invariance compares actual image intervals and requires a C1 map with nowhere-zero derivative, including endpoint derivatives. Positive derivative preserves future traversal; negative derivative reverses causal direction and produces a negative oriented original increment, not negative elapsed proper time.

Geodesic means affinely parametrized. For a nonconstant geodesic, an admissible parameter change preserves the geodesic equation exactly when it is affine. Constant geodesics remain constant under arbitrary admissible parameter changes.

The exponential domain consists of initial vectors whose maximal geodesic is defined at parameter 1. Normal charts use a star-shaped open subset where the exponential is a diffeomorphism. Straight radial-coordinate assertions apply while the radial initial vector remains in that subset, and impose no second-order vanishing or global completeness.

Clock readings, massive-body free fall, and geometric-optics null-ray propagation are adopted physical coupling assumptions in the smooth classical test-field regime. Physical histories need only be restrictions of maximal mathematical geodesics; no measured inputs or empirical verification are asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For a smooth four-manifold without boundary and a smooth symmetric pointwise nondegenerate covariant 2-tensor g, there is exactly one affine connection satisfying the displayed Koszul identity. It is torsion-free and g-compatible, every torsion-free g-compatible connection equals it, and its induced tensor derivative has the displayed component formula, commutes with contraction, and annihilates g and g inverse.

For the metric-selected connection of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, every (p,v) has a unique maximal geodesic on an open interval containing 0; its evaluation has an open domain and is smooth. For every real s,t, t belongs to I(p,sv) iff st belongs to I(p,v), with γ(p,sv)(t)=γ(p,v)(st). The exponential map is smooth on its open star-shaped domain, has differential identity at zero, and restricts to a diffeomorphism on a star-shaped open neighborhood of zero.

For the stated piecewise-C1 future timelike worldlines, proper-time increments are partition independent, additive, and strictly positive on nondegenerate intervals; the stated nowhere-zero-derivative reparametrizations obey the orientation-sensitive integral identities. For a C1 future timelike worldline, τ′=sqrt(-g(γ′,γ′))/c>0, and reparametrization by proper time has tangent U with g(U,U)=-c², with the stated piecewise and one-sided versions.

At every point of the stated Lorentzian four-manifold there is a smooth chart centered there with Γ=0, first metric derivatives zero, and metric matrix diag(-1,1,1,1). Exponential charts from any orthonormal tangent basis have the same identities and represent the stated radial portions of geodesics by straight lines; no second-derivative assertion is made.

On a star-shaped open exponential diffeomorphism domain W at p, g(exp_p(v))(dexp_v(v),dexp_v(w))=g_p(v,w) for every v∈W and w∈T_pM. Every stated piecewise-C1 future timelike curve from p remaining in exp_p(W) has length at most sqrt(-g_p(v_q,v_q)), with equality exactly for the stated monotone radial reparametrizations.

Adopt the assumptions that ideal clocks reproduce their future timelike worldlines' proper time, ideal freely falling massive test bodies follow future timelike metric-selected geodesics with g(U,U)=-c², and ideal light rays follow future null geodesics in the geometric-optics approximation, under the stated test-field scope and exclusions.

concerns.concern: Clause (a) permits k∈N₀∪{∞}, while clause (c) defines a 'C^k future timelike worldline' by requiring its velocity at every parameter value. Clause (b) defines that velocity for C1 curves. The k=0 case therefore needs an explicit differentiability requirement or an explicit k≥1 restriction; a merely continuous curve has no defined velocity under the preceding clauses.

alerts.finding: Fact L3 says 'a nonzero vector is future-directed exactly when g(V,∂t)<0'. The cited causal definitions apply this sign criterion to nonzero causal vectors. In the flat FLRW case c=a=1, V=∂t+2∂1 has g(V,∂t)=-1 but g(V,V)=3, so it is spacelike and receives no future-directed classification from those definitions. The actual ray is assumed null, but the factual sentence as written is overstrong.

Fact L5 attributes the length formula for the restriction of the locally absolutely continuous future causal curve σ to def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time. That definition expressly defines length only for future timelike worldlines and excludes null curves in clause (f). The broader Lebesgue length definition is available in lem-gr-normal-neighborhood-length-monotonicity, already a declared dependency; the cited supplier is narrower than the use.

The Statement introduces 'the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves' with the citation def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time. That supplier defines piecewise-C1 future timelike length and explicitly excludes null curves, whereas this item takes a supremum over the broader future causal class. The earlier lem-gr-normal-neighborhood-length-monotonicity supplies the relevant Lebesgue length definition.
